newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to ease limits on imports of Japanese fruit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to ease limits on imports of Japanese fruit.

text.p: Taiwan has agreed to ease limits on imports of Japanese apples, oranges and pears in a bid to speed up its entry to the World Trade Organisation (WTO), officials said on Tuesday.

"It is some sort of provisional arrangement before we join the WTO, and we will allow the import of a certain number of Japanese apples, oranges and pears," a senior official of the Board of Foreign Trade told Reuters by telephone.
He declined to provide details, but emphasised that Taiwan had no plans to totally remove the ban on such fruit upon becoming a member of the world trade body.
"That has to be done gradually. We will increase quotas (for their import) each year," he said.
Fuller details would be disclosed this week, he added.
Japan's news agency Kyodo reported on Tuesday that Taiwan had agreed to soon abolish restrictions on imports of Japanese apples, oranges and pears at Tokyo's request.
Japan's agriculture ministry was quoted by Kyodo as saying Taiwan granted the Japanese request to help secure Japan's support for its bid to enter the WTO.
